0.content: Zhongli is the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's most revered consultant. His evening lectures train her undertakers best, and he handles the extremely rare rites for departed adepti. Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned ("his personality is a bit dusty"), and in 6.3 said he would be the perfect employee if he could rein in his spending. Still, he is the person she trusts most. She has half-voiced a suspicion that he is not an ordinary man and then dropped it. Zhongli says he "cannot deal with that child", but the wiki notes he took the job because she interested him.

1.content: Soon after meeting the zombie Qiqi, Hu Tao decided that as her self-proclaimed true friend she should grant her eternal peace. She kidnapped Qiqi several times, each time calculating an auspicious hour and planning a proper cremation and tomb. Each time Baizhu arrived to find Qiqi stuffed in a bag with only her head poking out, watching Hu Tao dig a pit for the pyre. Hu Tao sent a letter apologising for not laying her to rest fast enough. Qiqi learned to remember hiding places just to escape her. Moved by Qiqi's will to live and her history, Hu Tao decided she was a rare exception to the natural order, and began to pamper her. Qiqi still calls her "Warm. Fake smile. Death." and says she despises her.

2.content: The owner of Bubu Pharmacy grew more set on achieving eternal life after meeting Qiqi, and Hu Tao finds that unacceptable. "Baizhu? Ugh, that guy..." Yet the pharmacy and the parlor are neighbours: when a life-and-death question cannot be settled in a few words, she invites him to dinner, and he comes. Over years of shared banquets they have become close friends who keep secrets from each other. Patients who die in his care are sent to a secluded cottage where Wangsheng's consultant performs the rites. Baizhu says he bears her no ill will and that she is the more wary one.

3.comment: Hu Tao: Xingqiu, Chongyun and Xiangling
3.content: Xingqiu came to Wangsheng on an auspicious day with a gift to meet the poet behind the Hilitune. His classical verse met her strange, catchy, chaotic verse, and she "beat the old master with untrained fists". They have composed paired verses ever since, one strict and one playful, with Chongyun dragged in as umpire. Xingqiu thinks one must ask what she is really after. Chongyun respects the parlor but boils at her cheeky "It's nothing you exorcists need to worry about" smile; she marvels at his pure yang. Xiangling is her favourite person to scare. Hu Tao keeps it in check in case Guoba toasts her, and pays her back with fermented plum blossoms and rare ingredients.

4.comment: Hu Tao: The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Border
4.content: Liyue's funeral house, run by the Hu Family for 77 generations. Its philosophy is that everyone deserves a dignified send-off whatever their wealth or standing, and that services are tailored to each client's wishes, whether quiet, lively or lavish. "The living give us Mora to see the dead on their way. We have a responsibility to both parties." It also keeps the secrets of the "border", a boundary world between life and death reached beyond Wuwang Hill, where Ley Lines go haywire and lingering spirits gather. Wangsheng escorts souls with unfinished business across.

5.content: Hu Tao met the Traveler and Paimon on Wuwang Hill and roped them into her business plans, assuming they were adventurers. Together they helped Meng's friend Big G pass on peacefully. At the border she asked the spirits about the Traveler's lost sibling; none had seen them, and she promised to keep looking. She invites the Traveler for tea, night walks and ghost-spotting, and teases them freely ("I'm so happy I could die! You're such a fantastic friend!").
